cs.AI / 1 / 2611.13161
Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
认知多智能体搜索与救援：面向协作机器人的语言接地分层强化学习
Sepideh Ravanbakhsh, Hamidreza Moradi
cs.AI · cs.CE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.
Chinese Translation
有效的搜索与救援（SAR）行动要求自主系统能够协调多个异构智能体、适应动态危险，并与人类任务意图保持一致。现有的语言引导强化学习（RL）方法主要关注单智能体指令遵循，缺乏在复杂、部分可观测环境中进行团队级协调的机制。本文提出一种基于语言接地分层强化学习（LG-HRL）的认知多智能体框架，该框架集成了自然语言理解、分层策略分解和共享认知工作空间，以在SAR场景中实现连贯的多智能体行为。人类指令由大语言模型（LLM）解释，并转化为结构化语义线索，用于指导UAV和UGV智能体间的高层策略选择与角色分配。引入形式化的语言接地多智能体分层决策过程（LG-MAHDP），以建模语义接地、分层控制与分布式协调之间的相互作用。在模拟灾难环境中的综合实验表明，LG-HRL将学习速度提高2.3倍，将协调一致性提高37%，并将子目标准确性和危险规避能力分别提高46%和31%。该系统实现了高出20-30%的受害者救援率，展现出涌现的角色专业化，并能立即适应人类的口头更新。消融研究证实，共享认知工作空间和语言接地二者对整体系统性能都至关重要。总体而言，这项工作为语言引导的多智能体SAR机器人建立了新范式，表明语义接地与分层推理相结合能够实现更安全、更高效且更具可解释性的自主救援行动。

cs.AI / 2 / 2611.13217
Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
Claude Code 作为手写大学考试智能体 AI 评分系统的可靠性
Rayed AlGhamdi
cs.AI · cs.CY
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
This study examines the reliability of Claude Code, an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 large language model, as a grading system for handwritten university exams. Four research questions addressed agreement with expert human grading on total scores (RQ1), agreement across five question types from multiple choice to evaluative judgement (RQ2), consistency across two independent grading sessions one week apart (RQ3), and the accuracy of AI-generated feedback (RQ4). Claude Code graded the 20-mark mid-term papers of 60 consenting students in a Saudi computer graphics course in a single agentic session, guided by three rubric files. Reliability was estimated on disjoint samples: 20 papers for RQ1, RQ2 and RQ4, and 15 papers for RQ3. Analyses used Pearson correlation, mean absolute error, Bland-Altman analysis, weighted Cohen kappa, intraclass correlation, and a four-category coding scheme separating diagnostic from confirmation feedback. The author, as the sole subject-matter expert for the course, provided the human benchmark, so the design assesses agreement with a domain-expert reference rather than inter-rater reliability. AI grading agreed strongly with human grading on totals (r = 0.97; MAE = 0.85 marks) with a small but significant AI-positive bias of 0.68 marks, showed excellent test-retest consistency (ICC = 0.96), and produced accurate feedback (92.8% diagnostic; 97.8% confirmation). Drawing items were the outlier on three of four measures. Three failure modes recurred: keyword matching without conceptual depth, selection-state ambiguity on corrected multiple-choice answers, and region-of-attention drift on hand-drawn diagrams. The findings suggest that AI grading at this capability level can assist instructors on objective and short-form items under structural safeguards but is not yet ready to replace instructor judgement at boundary cases or on drawing items.

cs.AI / 3 / 2611.13233
Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning
通过区分进行决策：面向医学推理的差异性证据
Yunpeng Xiao, Yuzhang Xie, Junhao Huang, Carl Yang, Xiao Hu, Kai Shu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly studied for clinical decision support, and medical question answering provides a testbed for evaluating this capability. In particular, medical multiple-choice questions (MCQs) reflect a core challenge in clinical decision-making: plausible options often share overlapping evidence, while only a few decisive factors distinguish the correct option from incorrect ones. However, existing retrieval-based and reasoning-oriented methods mainly focus on supplying broadly relevant knowledge or eliciting reasoning paths, rather than identifying the compact differential evidence that separates confusing alternatives. In this work, we present a retrieval-grounded differential evidence framework for medical MCQs. Our method extracts option-specific pieces of differential evidence and organizes them into concise evidence prompts for answer selection. This design better aligns external knowledge with differential reasoning while reducing irrelevant context. Experiments show consistent accuracy gains across multiple datasets and target LLMs. Ablation studies further show that our framework outperforms both directly using retrieved evidence chunks and closed-source LLM-generated general hints, and that its improvements are not solely explained by answer-proximal guidance, but are consistent with differential evidence serving as a compact aid for reasoning over competing alternatives. Our findings also offer insights for medical reasoning and other decision-making settings with multiple possible choices.
Chinese Translation
大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被研究用于临床决策支持，而医学问答为评估这一能力提供了试验平台。特别是，医学多项选择题（MCQs）反映了临床决策中的一个核心挑战：看似合理的选项往往共享重叠的证据，而只有少数决定性因素将正确选项与错误选项区分开来。然而，现有的基于检索和面向推理的方法主要关注提供广泛相关的知识或引出推理路径，而不是识别出能够区分令人困惑的备选项的紧凑差异性证据。在这项工作中，我们提出了一个面向医学多项选择题的基于检索的差异性证据框架。我们的方法提取选项特定的差异性证据片段，并将其组织成简洁的证据提示，用于答案选择。这种设计更好地将外部知识与差异性推理对齐，同时减少无关上下文。实验表明，在多个数据集和目标LLM上均获得了一致的准确率提升。消融研究进一步表明，我们的框架优于直接使用检索到的证据块以及闭源LLM生成的一般性提示，并且其改进不能仅由答案邻近引导来解释，而是与差异性证据作为在相互竞争的备选项之间进行推理的紧凑辅助手段相一致。我们的发现也为医学推理以及其他具有多个可能选择的决策场景提供了见解。

cs.AI / 4 / 2611.13312
Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent
面向通过 R2C-Agent 实现可扩展的、基于网络的 HIV 治疗与预防干预
Akseli Kangaslahti, Milind Tambe, Alastair van Heerden, Cheryl Johnson
cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) remains a pressing public health challenge worldwide. Targeting limited HIV prevention and treatment resources effectively with network-based algorithms is a long-standing problem with a rich history at AAMAS and other computational venues. However, optimizing targeted biomedical interventions for minimizing spread of HIV often requires observability of the contact network of HIV transmission risk behavior among individuals, which is prohibitively expensive to collect at scale. Peer referral networks, i.e., networks collected through a recursive peer referral process, are an alternative network class often used to study HIV in hidden populations that can be collected digitally at scale, but they deviate from the underlying contact network: referrals can follow non-risk social ties and participants accept only one referral, hiding contacts among already-recruited individuals. In this work, we first formalize the novel problem of planning network-based interventions to minimize HIV spread in the hidden contact network while observing only the peer referral network. Second, we implement R2C-Agent, a decision making agent for interventions that is designed around our new conditional graph diffusion model called Referral-to-Contact Diffusion (R2C-Diff). R2C-Diff positions the peer referral process as incremental corruption of the underlying contact network and learns to reverse it. R2C-Agent plans its interventions over contact networks sampled from R2C-Diff, so its decisions account for uncertainty about the hidden contact network. Finally, we conduct simulated experiments using real-world HIV network data that demonstrate that R2C-Agent empirically plans more effective interventions than baselines from interdisciplinary literature and highlight key tradeoffs and assumptions driving performance.
Chinese Translation
人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）仍然是全球紧迫的公共卫生挑战。使用基于网络的算法有效配置有限的 HIV 预防和治疗资源是一个长期存在的问题，在 AAMAS 和其他计算领域有着丰富的研究历史。然而，为最小化 HIV 传播而优化靶向生物医学干预，通常需要能够观测个体间 HIV 传播风险行为的接触网络，而大规模收集该网络的成本高得令人望而却步。同伴转介网络，即通过递归同伴转介过程收集的网络，是一类替代网络，常用于研究隐藏人群中的 HIV，并且可以以数字方式大规模收集，但它们偏离了底层接触网络：转介可能沿着非风险的社会关系进行，而且参与者只接受一次转介，从而隐藏了已招募个体之间的接触。在这项工作中，我们首先形式化了一个新问题：在仅观测同伴转介网络的情况下，规划基于网络的干预以最小化隐藏接触网络中的 HIV 传播。其次，我们实现了 R2C-Agent，这是一个用于干预的决策智能体，围绕我们新的条件图扩散模型 Referral-to-Contact Diffusion (R2C-Diff) 设计。R2C-Diff 将同伴转介过程定位为对底层接触网络的增量破坏，并学习逆转这一过程。R2C-Agent 在从 R2C-Diff 采样得到的接触网络上规划其干预，因此其决策考虑了对隐藏接触网络的不确定性。最后，我们使用真实世界的 HIV 网络数据进行模拟实验，结果表明 R2C-Agent 在经验上规划的干预比来自跨学科文献的基线更有效，并突出了驱动性能的关键权衡和假设。

cs.AI / 5 / 2611.13594
Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth
Transformer 可证明地学习图搜索：训练动力学与深度的指数级能力
Xutao Ma, Somayeh Sojoudi
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress on complex reasoning tasks, yet the mechanisms by which they acquire reasoning capabilities and the efficiency of their reasoning remain poorly understood. In this paper, we investigate the path-finding problem over directed graphs, a symbolic abstraction of multi-step reasoning. We first characterize the architectural requirements for this task, proving that one-layer transformers require $Ω(N^2)$ size on dense graphs to implement the key DFS child-selection primitive. While a two-layer transformer implements full DFS with $O(N\log(N))$ size. Thus, a second layer is necessary and sufficient for near-linear DFS reasoning. We then extend this expressivity analysis to deeper models: for every $k\geq3$, a $k$-layer transformer implements a bounded-reachability DFS policy with look-ahead horizon $1+2^{k-3}$, establishing an exponential increase in reachability horizon with depth. Finally, going beyond expressivity, given appropriately curated training data, we show that two-layer transformers can provably learn to execute DFS via gradient flow and generalize to unseen graphs. Together, our results provide a mechanistic account of how transformers implement graph search, how depth expands bounded look-ahead, and how such reasoning algorithms can emerge through training.
Chinese Translation
大型语言模型（LLMs）在复杂推理任务上取得了显著进展，但它们获得推理能力的机制以及其推理效率仍然鲜为人知。本文研究有向图上的路径寻找问题，这是多步推理的一种符号抽象。我们首先刻画该任务对架构的要求，证明单层 Transformer 在稠密图上需要 $Ω(N^2)$ 的规模才能实现关键的 DFS 子节点选择原语。而两层 Transformer 以 $O(N\log(N))$ 的规模实现完整的 DFS。因此，第二层对于近线性 DFS 推理是必要且充分的。随后，我们将这一表达能力分析推广到更深的模型：对于每个 $k\geq3$，一个 $k$ 层 Transformer 实现具有前瞻视野 $1+2^{k-3}$ 的有界可达性 DFS 策略，从而确立了可达性视野随深度呈指数增长。最后，超越表达能力，在给定适当整理的训练数据的情况下，我们表明两层 Transformer 可以通过梯度流可证明地学会执行 DFS，并泛化到未见过的图。总之，我们的结果提供了关于 Transformer 如何实现图搜索、深度如何扩展有界前瞻，以及此类推理算法如何通过训练涌现的机制性解释。

cs.AI / 6 / 2611.13651
DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
DrugCoding：面向药物发现的科学编程智能体
Junwei Hu, Zhuohao Lin, Kun Li, Hengnan Zhang
cs.AI · cs.MA
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Drug discovery involves multiple interconnected research stages, including molecular design, property prediction, and virtual screening. These processes are characterized by complex workflows, interdependent computational tasks, and diverse specialized tools, placing substantial demands on the coordination of scientific models and computational resources. However, existing large language model (LLM)-based scientific agents still face challenges in autonomous planning of complex tasks, adaptive selection of specialized models, and reliable execution of multi-stage scientific computations, limiting their effectiveness in automating complex drug discovery workflows. To address these challenges, we propose DrugCoding, a scientific programming agent system that integrates scientific task planning, adaptive model routing, multi-agent collaboration, and programmatic tool execution. DrugCoding enables autonomous task planning and dynamic model adaptation for complex research objectives. It can flexibly invoke specialized scientific models, autonomously generate and execute code according to task requirements, and leverage multi-agent collaboration to support efficient execution and reliable validation of complex scientific tasks. To evaluate DrugCoding's performance in scientific tool invocation and multi-stage task execution, we conduct multi-turn tool-calling experiments across diverse language models and scientific tool interfaces. Experimental results demonstrate that DrugCoding achieves an average session-level Pass@1 of 97.35% on the full benchmark, outperforming the strongest baseline, Codex, by 9.24%. On the challenging subset, DrugCoding achieves 97.92%, exceeding the strongest baseline.

cs.AI / 7 / 2611.13713
Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
迈向自主 RTL 与综合优化：基准测试与自我改进型智能体
Wenji Fang, Yao Lu, Jinghua Wang, Zhiyao Xie
cs.AI · cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

cs.AI / 8 / 2611.13850
Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
机器人运动学的与分类体系无关的神经符号接地
Bastien Dussard, Aur{é}lie Clodic, Guillaume Sarthou
cs.AI · cs.RO
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

cs.AI · cs.IR

Abstract
Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

Eoin M. Kenny, Salim I. Amoukou, Tom Bewley
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.

TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
TreeAgent：用于处理长层次数据的结构感知记忆智能体
Wei Gu, Weiwei Qi, Jiajun Tang, Tianhang Zheng, Bo Chen, Zhibo Zhang, Jinfei Liu, Kui Ren
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reasoning on later segments. To address these limitations, we propose TreeAgent, a structure-aware agent that uses the input hierarchy to guide both segment-wise context processing and access to past information. Specifically, TreeAgent constructs segments from complete subtrees and groups of adjacent sibling subtrees to preserve local structural relationships. We provide theoretical guarantees on segment counts to guide token budget selection toward matching the segment count of fixed-length segmentation. We further attach structural paths to the segments for the agent to identify their ancestors and hierarchical positions. We also introduce residual memory links from the segments of low-level children to the segments of high-level parents, enabling direct information flows beyond successive memory updates. We evaluate TreeAgent with four representative memory agents on eight retrieval and aggregation tasks. The inputs are derived from real-world application data in JSON, HTML, YAML, and JavaScript and range from 8K to 1M tokens. TreeAgent improves the average score across the four datasets for all four agents, with 3.61% performance gain on average.

Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
Hx2Dx：从病史采集到诊断——面向大语言模型对话式临床推理的多模态竞技场
Federico Ravenda, Mirko Cesarini, Daniele Montagnani, Volodymyr Karpenko, Antonietta Mira, Andrea Raballo
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) achieve expert-level diagnostic accuracy in static evaluations, where the model receives a curated vignette or case report that already condenses the diagnostically relevant findings. Such evaluations measure inference over already selected evidence; the evaluations do not account for the inquiry used to obtain it. In clinical practice, however, diagnosis is an iterative process of inquiry. Clinicians take the patient's history, or anamnesis (Hx), through targeted questioning, examine the patient, and request and interpret tests, progressively narrowing the differential until they reach a final diagnosis (Dx). We introduce Hx2Dx ARENA, an interactive benchmark of 1'000 clinical cases from the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM). Each case is a simulated encounter that proceeds from initial presentation through history taking and physical examination to diagnostic workup. We evaluate open- and closed-source LLMs under multiple configurations. Performance varies considerably across models in the interactive setting, and every model loses diagnostic accuracy relative to the static setting, where the full case is presented upfront. The ability to ask the right questions accounts for much of both the gap between models and the loss of accuracy: diagnosis improves as questions become more targeted and build a more complete clinical picture. LLMs thus reason well once the relevant data are available but remain limited in hypothesis-driven information gathering, in knowing what to ask in order to know. Closing this gap is a prerequisite for their safe integration into real-world diagnostic workflows.

BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions
BARS：未知分布下用于多数识别的预算感知带拒绝序贯采样
Shenxi Liu, Yiwei Li, Mingyang Zhao, Yuhang Tian, Kan Li
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Repeated sampling with majority selection is an effective means of enforcing self-consistency in large language models. Recently, a variant has also been introduced that terminates early to save costs when the output distribution is favorable. But it still cannot yield a correct confidence estimate from the answer distribution. For this issue, we formalize this as majority identification under an unknown distribution with a budget and a target error rate, and propose BARS, a sequential rule certifying the top-two gap and returning an early stop, a budgeted majority vote, or a refusal when feasibility cannot be established. A refusal is a statement about the rule and its budget, not a claim that a question is unanswerable, and it tells practitioners when to widen the budget or switch models. A certified mode carries proven bounds on the joint answering error and on refusing an instance the budget could handle, while a practical mode, used in our experiments, replaces them with empirical calibration. On synthetic instances drawn from known distributions over thousands of seeds, the difficulty-driven behavior is recovered and the price of the certified mode is measured.On GSM8K the practical mode draws 22.3\% fewer samples than fixed-8 sampling over the same pool, refused questions included, at the cost of declining 18.8\% of the questions. On MATH, it greatly improves the accuracy of its output answers into 82.5\% at the cost of honestly refusing to answer half of the difficult questions that the model itself is unable to solve.

Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
集中式与弥散式注意力头 Dropout 下自回归多步推理的崩溃
Karol Struniawski
cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). Error analysis reveals that Qwen failures reflect derivation errors within formatted responses (conditional accuracy drop of $-11.4$ pp), whereas in LLaMA $22.2\%$ of discordant losses lack a final answer format line (conditional gap narrows to $-5.0$ pp). These findings demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are particularly vulnerable to concentrated structural disruptions, providing empirical benchmarks for fault tolerance in transformer architectures.

LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
LM-SimBench：面向大语言模型训练模拟的统一框架、数据集与基准
Yu Dong, Hong Li, Qiang Sun, Xu Zhou, Jinbiao Huo, Qixiu Cheng, Zhiyuan Liu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale. Performance simulation offers a lower cost alternative, yet controlled comparisons among existing simulators remain difficult because they differ in the training stages they model and the workloads on which they are evaluated. We introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators. The framework decomposes simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule level aggregation, connecting execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets. Following this framework, we profile 23 model settings from 10 dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM families on an Ascend Neural Processing Unit (NPU) cluster. The resulting dataset contains 348 feasible configurations that jointly vary five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation, with six views spanning configuration, rank, operator, event, and kernel granularity. Evaluations of representative training simulators demonstrate how LM-SimBench supports comparisons of prediction accuracy, assessment of configuration selection, and diagnosis of prediction errors. Matched GPU-NPU experiments validate the cross-platform applicability of the collection and evaluation protocol and demonstrate NPU-guided GPU configuration selection.

Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
大语言模型中“通过思考学习”机制的认知映射
Dong Han, Jin Zhang, Kunyue Yang
cs.AI
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exhibit capabilities that resemble human Learning by Thinking (LbT), the acquisition of new insight through internal processes such as explanation and reasoning, without new external input. A systematic account of the cognitive mechanisms behind these capabilities, and of their limits, remains underdeveloped. This paper proposes a Cognitive LbT Framework that maps four mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) onto computational processes in LLMs. Drawing on representative methods, including chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts search, Self-Instruct, and self-taught reasoning, the analysis argues that selected methods can functionally approximate aspects of these mechanisms and can improve performance on some tasks without additional labeled examples, although this does not always constitute durable learning in model parameters. For example, Self-Instruct generated approximately 52,000 instructions from 175 seed tasks and reported a 33% absolute improvement on Super-NaturalInstructions (Y. Wang et al., 2023). The same mechanisms also produce characteristic failures, including hallucination diffusion, model collapse, concept drift, and high computational cost. These failures are not isolated technical defects but follow from four structural asymmetries between LLMs and human cognition: the identity of generator and monitor, closed learning loops without external grounding, symbolic rather than sensorimotor simulation, and the cost of inference-time computation. The framework yields testable propositions about when LbT in LLMs should succeed or fail and offers a structured basis for designing more reliable autonomous learning systems.

Wang et al., 2023）。这些机制同样会产生特征性失败，包括幻觉扩散、模型崩溃、概念漂移与高计算成本。这些失败并非孤立的技术缺陷，而是源于大语言模型与人类认知之间的四种结构性不对称：生成者与监控者的同一性、缺乏外部根基的闭环学习、符号性而非感觉运动性的模拟，以及推理时计算的成本。该框架就大语言模型中的 LbT 何时应当成功或失败提出了可检验的命题，并为设计更可靠的自主学习系统提供了结构化基础。

An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
基于能量的机器学习视角
Bo Dai, Yilun Du
cs.AI · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Energy-based models (EBMs) define a distribution through a scalar energy, $p_θ(x)\propto\exp(-E_θ(x))$, and are usually presented as one model family among many. This tutorial has a broader goal: beyond introducing EBMs, it uses them as a single lens that connects the different aspects of machine learning. Any EBM is specified by three choices, the energy, which determines what the model represents; the inference procedure, which samples from or optimizes the energy; and the learning method, which fits the energy to data. We first develop these components, including sampling, variational inference, and learning by maximum likelihood, noise contrastive estimation, pseudolikelihood, score matching, and adversarial training, and show that the learning methods share one contrastive structure. We then show that discriminative models, generative models such as GANs, normalizing flows, diffusion and autoregressive models, representation learning methods such as contrastive learning, word2vec, BERT, denoising auto-encoders, and diffusion representations, reinforcement learning with EBM policies and world models, inverse reinforcement learning, and planning, as well as inference-time computation with verifiers, are all EBMs that differ in these three choices, mostly in how they handle the partition function and sampling. This view explains existing methods, organizes them into a common framework, and suggests new algorithms by replacing one component while keeping the others, with composition of energies as a principled way to combine learned models at inference time.

基于能量的模型（EBMs）通过一个标量能量定义分布，$p_θ(x)\propto\exp(-E_θ(x))$，并且通常被作为众多模型族中的一种来介绍。本教程有一个更宽泛的目标：除了介绍EBMs之外，它还将EBMs作为一个单一的透镜，连接机器学习的不同方面。任何EBM都由三个选择来指定：能量，它决定模型表示什么；推断过程，它从能量中采样或优化能量；以及学习方法，它将能量拟合到数据。我们首先展开这些组成部分，包括采样、变分推断，以及通过最大似然、噪声对比估计、伪似然、得分匹配和对抗训练进行学习，并表明这些学习方法共享一种对比结构。然后我们表明，判别模型，生成模型如GANs、归一化流、扩散模型和自回归模型，表示学习方法如对比学习、word2vec、BERT、去噪自编码器和扩散表示，使用EBM策略和世界模型的强化学习、逆强化学习以及规划，还有使用验证器的推理时计算，都是在这三个选择上不同的EBM，主要在于它们如何处理配分函数和采样。这一视角解释了现有方法，将它们组织到一个共同框架中，并通过替换一个组成部分而保留其他组成部分来提示新算法，并将能量的组合作为在推理时组合已学习模型的一种有原则的方式。

ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
ReTrace：将使用工具的智能体蒸馏为无规划器工作流
Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya, Rohith Nama, Arushi Gupta, Carlos D. Castillo, Prathap Ramachandra, Xiaofan Jiang, Francesco Carbone
cs.AI · cs.LG · cs.MA
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

Tri-Stack-PIM: A Heterogeneous Multi-Die 3D-Integrated Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Efficient LLM Inference
Tri-Stack-PIM：一种用于高效LLM推理的异构多裸片3D集成存内计算架构
Shuao Jia, Zichao Ling, Chen Bai, Kang Zhao, Jianwang Zhai
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) inference during autoregressive decoding is fundamentally memory-bandwidth-bound. Existing three-dimensional (3D) stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures alleviate the off-chip bandwidth wall, yet remain constrained by several limitations: physical layer (PHY), controllers, and direct memory access (DMA) engines compete with arithmetic units for advanced-node base-die area; hybrid-bonding keep-out zones fragment the base-die floorplan and impede physical design; compute tiles built in a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) process are restricted to low logic density, capping achievable throughput; and nonlinear operations offloaded to the host reintroduce a communication bottleneck. We present Tri-Stack-PIM, a heterogeneous three-die architecture that resolves these tensions by dedicating a top DRAM die to storage, a middle buffer die on a mature process node to PHYs, DMA engines, and near-memory compute units, and a bottom base die on an advanced node exclusively to single-instruction-multiple-data (SIMD) multiply-accumulate (MAC) arrays. We further introduce a Unified Buffer-Aware Ready-based (UBAR) hardware out-of-order micro-operation scheduler that enforces cross-die dependency correctness at runtime while maximizing issue-slot utilization through a multi-term priority function, recovering up to 90% of the cycles that an in-order policy would forfeit. A joint architecture-dataflow co-exploration identifies Pareto-optimal configurations that reduce the energy-delay product (EDP) by 33-66x over naive parameter selection. Evaluated across multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention (MHA, GQA, MQA) mechanisms with batch sizes 1-32, Tri-Stack-PIM achieves geometric-mean speedups of 4.95x, 2.57x, and 1.68x across all three attention mechanisms and batch sizes over a graphics processing unit (GPU) baseline, AttAcc, and H2-LLM, respectively.

Uncovering the Memory Hierarchy of Modern NVIDIA GPUs for Accurate Simulation
揭示现代 NVIDIA GPU 的内存层次结构以实现精确模拟
Ziwen Wang, Jiapeng Zhou, Changxi Liu, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen
cs.AR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Emerging artificial intelligence workloads, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), place unprecedented demands on GPU memory systems. Consequently, architectural innovations increasingly target the memory system to alleviate these bottlenecks. However, existing works still rely on outdated memory hierarchy models that fail to capture the complexities of modern hardware. This fidelity gap leads to inaccurate characterization and could misguide optimization strategies. To bridge this gap, we present GemAtlas, the first systematic reverse engineering of the memory hierarchy in modern NVIDIA GPUs. By developing fine-grained SASS-level benchmarking, we expose critical, previously undocumented micro-architectural details across different cache levels, including cache set associativity, slice-routing and set-indexing hash functions, replacement policies, coherence behavior, and interconnect topologies. We integrate these discovered micro-architecture details into the state-of-the-art GPU simulation framework. The final results demonstrate that GemAtlas reduces the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 31.69% to 22.24% on average across four GPUs. Specifically, GemAtlas reduces the MAPE from 34.04% to 23.98% for real-world LLM operators.

TAPCO-G: LLM-Guided Design-Adaptive Timing and Power Co-Optimization with Graph-Based Physical Priors

Wuqian Tang, Zixiao Wang, Che-Chien Lin, Fong-Hua Fu, Laura Angélica Shion-Korsak, Xinyun Zhang, Bei Yu, Chun-Yao Wang
cs.AR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Post-placement timing and power co-optimization is critical to meeting setup timing targets and reducing power within placement constraints. A cell replacement can improve timing along one path while increasing power or reducing slack on others. Conventional optimizers follow fixed rules for scheduling and accepting repairs, limiting their ability to address design-specific bottlenecks. A large language model (LLM) can propose changes to these rules, but on its own it cannot reliably estimate how a cell replacement affects endpoint slack and power. TAPCO-G combines LLM-guided optimizer adaptation with graph-based physical priors to evaluate candidate cell replacements. The outer loop tunes tool settings using physical-design feedback and revises executable repair policies when tuning stalls. The inner loop anchors delay estimates to static timing analysis snapshots, accounts for upstream driver-load changes, and propagates delay shifts to timing endpoints. It combines these estimates with coarse-to-fine power screening to prioritize candidates for physical trials. TAPCO-G produced placement-legal, logic-equivalent implementations and outscored CERBERUS on all eight ASAP7 benchmarks from the MLCAD 2026 Contest, with a mean quality score gain of 5.516 points, and scored 21.648 points higher than TAPCO on average. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed co-optimization framework.

Catch It Where It Happens: Real Time Error Correction During LLM Reasoning
在错误发生处捕捉：LLM 推理过程中的实时错误纠正
Rotem Elimelech, Michael Shalyt, Ido Kaminer
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trusted with mathematical, scientific and engineering work, yet their mistakes are often confidently written and hard to spot. A single wrong step tends to propagate, making the model waste inference tokens following a false premise. Existing safeguards either check only the final answer and restart from scratch, or rely on a verifier LLM that competes for GPU capacity and slows down response time. We propose online, deterministic verification: many kinds of reasoning steps can be validated by code, so a step can be verified in real time, as it is written, without any model call or GPU use. Whenever a check fails, we point out the mistake and let the model continue from the same spot. We demonstrate this approach on symbolic mathematics, where derivations already contain explicit expressions that a computer algebra system can check in milliseconds. Tested on the ASyMoB benchmark with three open-weights models, our online validation improves accuracy by 1.4-5.6 percentage points, corresponding to a 1.8-14.9% net reduction in incorrect answers, while increasing token usage by only 6-7%. Because the verifier is independent of the model, the approach complements progress in LLMs rather than competing with it: every new model can benefit immediately, and the benefit grows as deterministic checkers extend to more kinds of reasoning steps.

cs.CL / 23 / 2611.13270
What drives the emergence of symbolic mechanisms in large language models?
是什么驱动了大语言模型中符号机制的出现？
Melody Zixuan Li, Taylor Webb
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent work has identified a set of emergent symbolic mechanisms that support abstract reasoning in large language models, but it remains unclear what factors drive the emergence of these mechanisms. To address this question, we trained neural networks from scratch on abstract sequence tasks, varying both architectural and data distributional factors, and investigated the effects of these factors on the emergence of symbolic mechanisms. Using representational, attentional, and causal mediation analyses, we first confirmed that transformer-based language models trained from scratch on our task developed symbolic mechanisms. We then found that, across multiple axes of data diversity, greater diversity produced stronger symbolic signatures. Surprisingly, the same signatures emerged in modified transformer architectures and even multilayer perceptrons, indicating that architectural inductive biases are not necessary for the development of symbolic mechanisms. We also observed consistent patterns in an entity-attribute binding task. Together, these findings identify data diversity, not architecture, as the primary driver of emergent symbolic computation in neural networks.
Chinese Translation
近期工作已经识别出一组支撑大语言模型抽象推理的涌现符号机制，但这些机制的出现由哪些因素驱动仍不清楚。为回答这一问题，我们在抽象序列任务上从零开始训练神经网络，改变架构因素和数据分布因素，并考察这些因素对符号机制出现的影响。通过表征分析、注意分析和因果中介分析，我们首先确认，在我们的任务上从零开始训练的基于 Transformer 的语言模型发展出了符号机制。随后我们发现，在数据多样性的多个维度上，更大的多样性产生了更强的符号特征。令人惊讶的是，在修改后的 Transformer 架构中，甚至多层感知机中，也出现了相同的特征，这表明架构性归纳偏置并不是符号机制发展所必需的。我们还在实体—属性绑定任务中观察到了一致模式。总之，这些发现确定数据多样性——而非架构——是神经网络中涌现符号计算的主要驱动因素。

Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts
测量社会科学概念的大语言模型标注中的定义敏感性
Bogdan Mamaev, Qizhou Wang, Christopher Leckie, Matteo Vergani
cs.CL · cs.CY
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content. However, concepts such as hate speech, fake news, and terrorism typically have several theoretically defensible competing definitions. It is also unknown whether the model actually applied the definition to provide the label or the label was based on the model's pretrained notion of the concept. To test this, we have the model annotate the same texts twice, each time with a different definition. We call the disagreement between the two sets of annotations definition sensitivity. As a control, we paraphrase one definition but leave its requirements unchanged - the disagreement between the annotations with the two wordings becomes the paraphrase floor. Across six concepts and three LLMs, a swap of competing definitions always changes more annotations, on average, than a paraphrase. This shows that the annotations depend on the prompted definition, so any set of annotations should be interpreted together with the definition that produced it. The LLM annotator's definition sensitivity and its paraphrase floor should both be reported in such work.

Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis
描绘教师对利用人工智能作弊的态度：一项基于论坛分析的探索性研究
Iman Mohammadi, Ali Keramati, Sina Rismanchian
cs.CL · cs.CY
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
In teaching and learning environments, cheating and the violation of academic integrity have always been one of the challenges, involving different levels of concerns such as administrative, personal knowledge, learning, and equity. The introduction of large language models has brought cheating in dialogue to the forefront, given the apparent capabilities of these models to complete students' academic assignments. This study aims to leverage recent dialogues among university professors about cheating with Generative AI to better understand their beliefs about academic honesty. In doing so, we analyze a corpus of 2.01 million posts (threads and comments) in the r/Professors subreddit discussing cheating after the release of ChatGPT, providing a better understanding of teachers' motivations to discourage cheating and the strategies they use to do so. We synthesize the why and how of addressing cheating to identify caveats about the future of AI and academic integration.

cs.CL / 26 / 2611.13426
BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
BioMem：面向生物医学大语言模型智能体的智能体记忆
Mingchen Li, Yongkang Xiao, Rumeng Li, Rui Zhang, Hong Yu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in biomedical applications, while agentic memory systems have emerged as a promising approach to preserving and utilizing information across tasks and interactions. However, a fundamental question remains: how effectively and reliably do these systems retain, retrieve, update, and utilize biomedical information? In this study, we systematically investigate agentic memory in the biomedical domain, focusing on task effectiveness, retrieval quality, information fidelity, and long-term robustness. We evaluate five memory approaches across four LLMs in three representative settings: biomedical knowledge reasoning, clinical prediction, and long-term conversational memory. Our analyses reveal how memory construction, evidence relevance, and conversational history shape downstream biomedical performance, highlighting the distinct challenges of retrieving relevant information, preserving its fidelity, and effectively utilizing it for reasoning. Building on these findings, we introduce Hybrid Memory Retrieval and Utilization (HMRU), a training-free framework that jointly enhances evidence accessibility and task-aware utilization to improve biomedical reasoning and long-term conversational memory. HMRU achieves an average relative improvement of 8.6% across biomedical question-answering and conversational memory benchmarks, with additional gains in selected clinical prediction tasks. It further reduces conversational answer errors by 24.9% and closes 48.0% of the performance gap to full-context inference. Our findings provide a systematic characterization of biomedical agentic memory and practical insights into developing more effective and reliable memory-augmented LLM systems.

大语言模型（LLMs）在生物医学应用中已展现出相当大的潜力，而智能体记忆系统已成为一种有前景的方法，用于跨任务和交互保留并利用信息。然而，一个根本性问题仍然存在：这些系统在保留、检索、更新和利用生物医学信息方面究竟有多有效、多可靠？在本研究中，我们系统性地考察生物医学领域中的智能体记忆，重点关注任务有效性、检索质量、信息保真度和长期稳健性。我们在三种代表性设置中，跨四个LLM评估了五种记忆方法：生物医学知识推理、临床预测和长期对话记忆。我们的分析揭示了记忆构建、证据相关性和对话历史如何塑造下游生物医学性能，并突出了检索相关信息、保持其保真度以及有效利用其进行推理方面的不同挑战。基于这些发现，我们引入了混合记忆检索与利用（HMRU），这是一个无需训练的框架，联合增强证据可访问性和任务感知利用，以改进生物医学推理和长期对话记忆。HMRU在生物医学问答和对话记忆基准上实现了平均8.6%的相对提升，并在选定的临床预测任务中带来额外增益。它进一步将对话答案错误降低了24.9%，并缩小了与全上下文推理之间48.0%的性能差距。我们的发现提供了对生物医学智能体记忆的系统性刻画，并为开发更有效、更可靠的记忆增强LLM系统提供了实践性见解。

Framing-Induced Vulnerability in Large Language Models: Evidence from Chinese News Headlines
大语言模型中的框架诱发脆弱性：来自中文新闻标题的证据
Mo Zhou, Yiwei Zhang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models increasingly evaluate, route, and moderate news, so a model's judgment of a headline has become a gatekeeping decision. We ask whether that judgment follows the fact being reported or the way the fact is framed. We combine an ecological audit of 63,926 Chinese news headlines with a controlled experiment. The experiment covers 30 real events, 30 synthetic events, and 29 natural headline pairs, tested on four Chinese models. Changing only the headline frame shifted both perceived misleadingness and event severity, and the direction and ordering of the shifts were the same for DeepSeek, MiMo, Dots, and LongCat. Emotionally intensified headlines raised severity ratings by 0.65 to 0.88 points, whereas positively reframed headlines lowered them by 0.34 to 0.52 points. Supplying the article body reduced this severity bias by 54 to 80 percent, and all four reductions were significant at p < .01. A small human reference study showed the same direction of effect. Headline-only LLM evaluation therefore carries a measurable robustness gap, and framing sensitivity belongs among the reliability properties that deployment and governance check.

An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
一个证据可追溯的大型语言模型临床推理基准
Zhiqun Zhao, Xiaodong Yang, Bruce Gu, Ming Li, Yi Fu, Song Li, Qi Mei, Zhi Liu, Kai Zhang, Kexue Fu, Jing Wu, Xiaofei Lu, Yule Li, Zheng Wang, Haiquan Lu, Xiaoming Wu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Benchmark scores for medical large language models (LLMs) are difficult to interpret when scoring criteria cannot be traced to clinical evidence. Here we developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB; https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/), comprising 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels: guideline knowledge, standardized clinical scenarios and real-world laboratory scenarios. Each criterion stating a medical claim is linked to a versioned source-text span. Across ten LLMs, the Evidence Trace Score (ETS) was 0.975-0.997 for guideline knowledge, 0.292-0.658 for standardized scenarios and 0.182-0.447 for real-world scenarios, and rankings varied across levels. For real-world scenarios, scores for identifying clinical information (mean, 0.770) exceeded those for matching evidence (0.165) or formulating recommendations (0.160). On 1,296 criterion-level judgments, automated grading agreed with the majority vote of three physicians (macro-F1, 0.930; 95% confidence interval, 0.915-0.945), although agreement was lower for evidence application. These findings from Chinese-language materials indicate that guideline recall does not ensure patient-specific evidence use and do not establish clinical effectiveness.

IFRS Compliance Verification: An Open Multi-LLM Benchmark and Content-Conditioned Ensemble Classifier
IFRS合规性验证：一个开放的多LLM基准与内容条件化集成分类器
Aghoghomena Akasukpe, Li Yang, Xinyao Zhou, Chen Shen, Miguel Vargas Martin
cs.CL · cs.IR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Verifying corporate financial disclosures against the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is a core auditing task in which experts cross-reference disclosures with hundreds of fine-grained regulatory paragraphs: a laborious, costly, and error-prone process that motivates growing interest in large language models (LLMs) as compliance assistants. Yet single-model accuracy remains insufficient for high-stakes use, and naive ensembling is vulnerable to systematic per-model biases that can drag aggregate accuracy below that of the strongest individual annotator. This gap is addressed with a multi-stage framework, supported by a new benchmark of 19,998 IFRS regulation-disclosure pairs comprising 11,161 unanimous multi-LLM labels and 8,837 human annotations on items where the LLMs disagreed. The framework couples a three-stage domain-adapted sentence embedding pipeline (BERT masked language modeling on SEC EDGAR filings, unsupervised TSDAE and SimCSE adaptation, and supervised contrastive alignment) with a learned ensemble classifier that fuses frozen embeddings and LLM probability features from GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, and Gemini 2.5 Pro via Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) optimized gradient-boosted trees. On the disagreement set, the ensemble achieves 81.7% weighted F1, exceeding the strongest single LLM by 10.4 points and majority voting by 14.6 points, and outperforms eleven unsupervised aggregation baselines; the retrieval pipeline attains Recall@15 of 45.3% on unseen regulations. The dataset, model checkpoints, annotation platform, and classifier implementation will be publicly released.

cs.CL / 30 / 2611.13615
Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control
Synapse-Control：通过轻量级运行时控制使智能体经验可付诸行动
Zhiyuan Huang, Shengan Zheng, Chenghu Yang, Song Zhang, Lingyun Li, Chen Yu, Weiquan Huang, Linpeng Huang
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model agents reuse execution experience to improve reliability on complex tool-based tasks. Systems such as Sentry call large models to generate failure diagnoses before retrieving advice, adding inference cost to experience reuse. We present Synapse-Control, an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects advice and determines when to send it to the task-executing model. Rules shortlist relevant advice, and a lightweight 1.7B classifier fine-tuned on teacher-labeled state-suggestion pairs scores those candidates instead of generating a diagnosis. Micro-contracts encode reusable interface checks, such as required arguments or valid options, without prescribing complete task programs. A Prompt Value Table records earlier guidance and feedback to limit repeated suggestions through cooldown and token-budget checks. Across 1,308 attempts per method in AppWorld and WebShop, Synapse-Control achieves 270 successes (29.8% more than Base), replaces 4,987 generative diagnosis calls, and reduces auxiliary control time relative to Sentry by 50.2% and 51.0%, respectively.
Chinese Translation
大型语言模型智能体复用执行经验，以提升基于工具的复杂任务的可靠性。Sentry 等系统在检索建议之前调用大型模型生成失败诊断，从而为经验复用增加了推理成本。我们提出 Synapse-Control，这是一种智能体运行时，其轻量级控制平面负责选择建议，并决定何时将建议发送给执行任务的模型。规则会对相关建议进行初筛，而一个基于教师标注的状态-建议对微调的轻量级 1.7B 分类器会对这些候选建议进行打分，而不是生成诊断。微契约编码可复用的接口检查，例如必需参数或有效选项，而不规定完整任务程序。提示值表记录先前的指导与反馈，通过冷却和 token 预算检查来限制重复建议。在 AppWorld 和 WebShop 中每种方法各 1,308 次尝试上，Synapse-Control 分别取得 270 次成功（比 Base 多 29.8%），取代了 4,987 次生成式诊断调用，并将辅助控制时间相对于 Sentry 分别减少了 50.2% 和 51.0%。

cs.CL / 31 / 2611.13675
OpticalRAG: Pixel-Space Compression for Token-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
OpticalRAG：面向令牌高效检索增强生成的像素空间压缩
Senhao Liu, Yuheng Zhang, Chunyu Wei, Yueguo Chen, Xinran Zhang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is bottlenecked by the token budget of large language models: feeding long documents into the context window is expensive, while aggressive textual compression discards fine-grained information that is irreversibly lost in a one-dimensional token sequence. We argue that this bottleneck is not fundamental to information density but to the choice of compression \emph{modality}. Modern visual encoders can pack the contents of a rendered text page into roughly a hundred visual tokens with little semantic loss, opening a new compression-fidelity tradeoff that purely textual methods cannot reach. We present \textbf{OpticalRAG}, a framework that renders documents as page images, encodes them with a frozen vision encoder, and distills the retrieved visual tokens into as few as $16$ injected tokens before passing them to the LLM. Two ingredients make this work without expensive cross-modal training: (i) \emph{Encoder-Bridged Retrieval}, which projects text-query states into the visual feature space of the frozen encoder, through a projection shared with the compressor, to retrieve visual tokens from a text query, with no contrastive training; and (ii) \emph{Query-Driven Distillation}, a lightweight cross-attention compressor that condenses the retrieved visual tokens into a small set of query-conditioned prefix tokens. On LongBench-v2, BAMBOO, and LooGLE-v2, OpticalRAG achieves the best compression-aware accuracy (CAP) on all three benchmarks while injecting only $16$ tokens, and improves the closed-book Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone by $5.17$ points on LongBench-v2.Code is available at https://github.com/brighterr/OpticalRAG.

检索增强生成（RAG）受到大语言模型令牌预算的瓶颈限制：将长文档输入上下文窗口代价高昂，而激进的文本压缩会丢弃细粒度信息，这些信息在一维令牌序列中会不可逆地丢失。我们认为，这一瓶颈并非信息密度的根本问题，而是压缩模态选择的问题。现代视觉编码器可以将渲染后的文本页面内容打包为大约一百个视觉令牌，而语义损失很小，从而开辟了纯文本方法无法达到的新的压缩—保真度权衡。我们提出 OpticalRAG，一个将文档渲染为页面图像、用冻结的视觉编码器对其进行编码，并在将检索到的视觉令牌传给 LLM 之前将其蒸馏为少至 $16$ 个注入令牌的框架。两个要素使这一方法无需昂贵的跨模态训练即可奏效：（i）编码器桥接检索（Encoder-Bridged Retrieval），它通过一个与压缩器共享的投影，将文本查询状态投影到冻结编码器的视觉特征空间中，从而从文本查询中检索视觉令牌，且无需对比训练；（ii）查询驱动蒸馏（Query-Driven Distillation），一种轻量级交叉注意力压缩器，将检索到的视觉令牌压缩为一小组以查询为条件的前缀令牌。在 LongBench-v2、BAMBOO 和 LooGLE-v2 上，OpticalRAG 在仅注入 $16$ 个令牌的情况下，在全部三个基准上取得最佳的压缩感知准确率（CAP），并在 LongBench-v2 上将闭卷 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 主干模型提升了 $5.17$ 分。代码可在 https://github.com/brighterr/OpticalRAG 获取。

diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
We present Alania-2, a Turkish text-to-speech (TTS) system with two built-in voices, voice design from text descriptions, and two kinds of voice cloning. Alania-2 is a 488M-parameter model with the VoxCPM architecture, which generates continuous audio latents with a diffusion head on top of a language-model backbone. We train it from scratch on 18,195 hours of Turkish speech, 90% of which is synthetic speech produced by a larger teacher model and filtered automatically. A text normalizer rewrites numbers, abbreviations and foreign names into the words a Turkish speaker would say; without it, none of 96 test sentences with digits kept all its critical parts, such as an amount or a date, through synthesis and speech recognition, against 86 with it. On Freya-TR-Eval, a public benchmark of 495 Turkish sentences scored with automatic speech recognition, Alania-2 reaches a word error rate of 1.44%, compared with 5.99% for our previous system. On its built-in voices, it comes within half a point of character error rate of a 2.3B-parameter model at under a quarter of the size, and a 7.6M-parameter single-voice model trained with the same recipe matches the most intelligible systems we measured, which suggests that training data matters more for intelligibility than model size. We also report practical findings on voice cloning: conditioning on the reference audio alone, rather than continuing it, cuts skipped words from 21.9% to 1.7%; 20-30 seconds of reference audio works best; and a low-rank adapter trained in about two minutes raises speaker similarity well above instant cloning. Finally, we describe inference-engine changes that bring first audio down to 32 ms for a single stream. We release our evaluation harness and three Turkish speech and text datasets.

Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
超越被动模仿：面向语言模型的同策略中期训练蒸馏
Ruize Zheng, Xuyang Liu, Siyu Ren, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Linfeng Zhang
cs.CL · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Continual pre-training (CPT) adapts large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains, yet its standard next-token prediction (NTP) objective treats every corpus token as a fixed target, regardless of its utility to the current model. In a controlled study on the same 1B-token mathematical corpus, we observe sharply different outcomes across base models: NTP improves Llama-3.2-3B's performance on mathematical benchmarks but substantially degrades Qwen3-1.7B-Base's performance, indicating that, under a fixed training recipe, the same training sequences can have model-dependent effects. To address this problem, we introduce On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD), which reformulates mid-training from offline text imitation into active, query-driven knowledge acquisition. At selected anchor positions, OPMD samples trajectories from the evolving student policy and applies dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher, training the model on states it actually visits rather than only on ground-truth prefixes. This on-policy objective reduces the training-generation mismatch of teacher-forced NTP. On MATH-500 and Minerva, OPMD improves the Qwen student over its base performance and outperforms the evaluated NTP baseline, which degrades on both benchmarks. OPMD integrates into CPT pipelines without added inference-time overhead and offers a model-aware alternative to passive domain adaptation.

Beyond Fluent Responses: Finding User Dissatisfaction in Human-AI Interactions
超越流畅回复：在人机交互中发现用户不满
Yuka Saito, Ikumi Numaya, Jun Suzuki, Reina Akama
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As large language models generate increasingly high-quality responses, recent work on response evaluation has moved beyond response-centered criteria, such as correctness and coherence, toward user-centered criteria, including user preferences and perceived usefulness. This shift is fundamentally important for developing technologies that are truly useful to real-world users. While conventional response evaluation quantifies the quality of the response itself, users' satisfaction in real conversations also depends on their subjective preferences and perceptions of usefulness, which do not necessarily align with response quality. This study investigates whether such user-centered signals can be detected from conversational text. Specifically, we analyze user utterances with self-reported dissatisfaction labels to examine whether user dissatisfaction in text can be detected. In English interaction, models using user utterances exceeded the 17.8% dissatisfaction label prevalence in AUPRC by up to 15 percentage points. These results suggest that user utterances reveal cues to implicit dissatisfaction. Furthermore, changes from the immediately preceding user utterance may improve dissatisfaction detection, with anomaly detection methods appearing particularly effective.

MISO-BR: An Open Corpus for Misogyny Detection in Brazilian Portuguese
MISO-BR：一个用于巴西葡萄牙语厌女内容检测的开放语料库
Fábio A. S. Passos, Péricles B. C. Miranda, Ana Paula Cavalcanti
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Misogyny is among the most prevalent forms of online hate speech directed at Brazilian users, yet open and auditable resources dedicated to it in Brazilian Portuguese remain scarce. We introduce MISO-BR, an open, documented and versioned corpus of 896 balanced social media texts annotated for binary misogyny, released with its construction protocol and reproducible baselines. The corpus combines lexicon- and target-guided scraping from X with items imported from OLID-BR, a large language model triage stage whose prompt and decoding parameters are released, and manual annotation by three annotators following a written guide. Inter-annotator reliability reaches a Fleiss' kappa of 0.788 over 816 items. Under a single fixed protocol we compare four classical classifiers (Multinomial and Bernoulli Naive Bayes, a linear SVM and a random forest) with fine-tuned BERTimbau Base and Large. The classical models cluster between 0.651 and 0.676 macro-F1 and are precision-oriented but recall-poor. The transformers reach 0.833 macro-F1 and accuracy (Wilson 95% CI for accuracy [0.77, 0.88]), a gap of roughly 16 points, while Base and Large are indistinguishable on the test set despite a 2.6x difference in training cost. We argue that the value of the resource lies less in its headline scores than in the auditability of its pipeline, and we state three limits that users must reckon with: the artificial class balance, whose effect on precision under realistic prevalence we quantify; the association between provenance and label, which the released source field makes measurable; and the selection bias induced by lexicon-guided sampling and automatic triage. The corpus, annotation guide, models and experimental scripts are publicly available.

From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
从偏见到位置性：面向大语言模型的批判性语法
Dave Murray-Rust, Elisa Giaccardi, Federico Bomba, Maria Luce Lupetti
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.HC
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to''. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails. We argue that positionality -- the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said -- is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? Against the vendors' answer of nowhere and the seductive possibility of everywhere, we argue that when a model is taken as-if speaking, it speaks from somewhere, and this means positionality can describe models, and the way they are believed beyond their warrant, even though they are not accountable speakers. A model's positionality is laminar -- laid down across corpus, tuning, system prompt, application and the live conversation. We separate three sets of factors: the positionality of a model's creators, the behaviour they intend for it, and the behaviour it enacts, and situate current work within this matrix. This lets us highlight what each stratum inherits from the one below, with ruptures and collapses where that inheritance is disavowed. We then return to where models speak from, and discuss the implications for how models are made, read and held accountable.

偏见已成为理解机器学习系统做什么以及我们应如何与之相处的默认视角。偏见归根结底是对标准的偏离；在决策系统中，我们可以从外部提供标准：一项法律、一个受保护属性、一个基准、一种统计性质。然而，即便在那里，“有偏”也常被用作简写，而未说明所采取的位置是什么——一个沉默的“相对于”。在语言模型的一般使用中，没有任何东西提供标准：没有可审计的决策，也没有反事实输出，因此这种简写失效了。我们认为，位置性——任何言说所出自的、有处所的、被明确表述的、被拥有的且可争辩的位置——是更好的语法，用以表述这些模型如今迫使我们面对的问题：谁在说话，从何处说？针对供应商给出的“无处”这一答案以及“处处”这一诱人可能性，我们认为，当模型被当作仿佛在言说时，它是从某处言说的；这意味着位置性可以描述模型，也可以描述它们被超出其担保范围地相信的方式，尽管它们并不是可问责的言说者。模型的位置性是层状的——横跨语料库、调优、系统提示、应用和实时对话层层铺设而成。我们区分三组因素：模型创造者的位置性、他们为其意图的行为，以及它实际实施的行为，并将当前工作置于这一矩阵之中。这使我们能够突出每一层从下一层继承了何种内容，并在这种继承被否认之处标出断裂与崩塌。随后，我们回到模型从何处言说这一问题，并讨论其对模型如何被制造、解读和问责的意涵。

Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
模糊块边界：面向高效扩散语言模型的重叠块去噪
Amir Mann, Jonathan Fhima, Shaked Brody, Or Avitan, Asif Zamir, Shahar Tsiper, Niv Nayman
cs.CL · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have emerged as effective alternatives to autoregressive models for latency-critical tasks, enabling faster token generation. Recent advances employ block diffusion with self-editing capabilities, where each block refines tokens iteratively before advancing to the next one. Yet each block is only as fast as its slowest token, and the next block cannot start before it. We suggest Blurring the Block Boundaries (B3), a novel method with which two blocks are refined in parallel within a shared forward pass. B3 calibrates itself on the fly, opening the next block only once the model is ready to start generating it. It is a training-free and hyperparameter-free acceleration method which seamlessly integrates within any self-editing block diffusion model. Evaluated on state-of-the-art DLMs across 10 diverse datasets spanning varied tasks and difficulty levels, B3 results in on par generation quality and 11.5-14.5% speedup compared to the base model, pushing the Pareto frontier for latency-quality trade-offs in DLM inference.

cs.CR / 38 / 2611.13577
TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
TERM：通过熵引导残差调制的无目标越狱防御
Yunkai Dang, Wanyu Zhang, Meiyi Zhu, Qi Fan, Tianyu Ding, Wenbin Li
cs.CR · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across diverse applications, making both safety and utility essential for reliable deployment. Jailbreak attacks use diverse forms of adversarial prompting to bypass alignment safeguards and induce LLMs to generate harmful responses. Some representation-based defenses regulate internal activations using predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. However, adapting intervention to each input without a predefined representational target while limiting over-refusal remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM), an inference-time defense that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to guide adaptive modulation of the model's own residual updates. Attention patterns vary across prompts and decoding steps, making raw entropy values difficult to interpret as a consistent signal for intervention. We therefore calibrate attention entropy against each prompt's own prefill baseline to establish an input-specific reference for reducing unnecessary intervention on benign requests. Adaptive scale normalization and temporal accumulation then account for differences in deviation scale and persistence to determine intervention strength. The resulting signal controls bounded scaling of the model's own residual updates, without relying on a predefined safety direction. We compare our method with seven defenses on seven jailbreak attacks and two over-refusal benchmarks across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models, including Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B. Results show our method improves jailbreak robustness while maintaining low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests with modest inference overhead.

Haoyi Wu, Yunkai Dang, Wanyu Zhang, Lei Wang, Wenbin Li
cs.CR · cs.CL
large language model

Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across diverse applications, making both safety and utility essential for reliable deployment. Jailbreak attacks use diverse forms of adversarial prompting to bypass alignment safeguards and induce LLMs to generate harmful responses. Some representation-based defenses regulate internal activations using predefined steering directions or learned safety regions. However, adapting intervention to each input without a predefined representational target while limiting over-refusal remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM), an inference-time defense that uses prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to guide adaptive modulation of the model's own residual updates. Attention patterns vary across prompts and decoding steps, making raw entropy values difficult to interpret as a consistent signal for intervention. We therefore calibrate attention entropy against each prompt's own prefill baseline to establish an input-specific reference for reducing unnecessary intervention on benign requests. Adaptive scale normalization and temporal accumulation then account for differences in deviation scale and persistence to determine intervention strength. The resulting signal controls bounded scaling of the model's own residual updates, without relying on a predefined safety direction. We compare our method with seven defenses on seven jailbreak attacks and two over-refusal benchmarks across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma models, including Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 32B. Results show our method improves jailbreak robustness while maintaining low over-refusal on benign safety-sensitive requests with modest inference overhead.

MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
MOAI：面向非交互式安全 Transformer 推理的模块优化架构
Linru Zhang, Xiangning Wang, Jun Jie Sim, Zhicong Huang, Jiahao Zhong, Huaxiong Wang, Pu Duan, Kwok-Yan Lam
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Privacy concerns have been raised in Large Language Models (LLM) inference when models are deployed in Cloud Service Providers (CSP). Homomorphic encryption (HE) offers a promising solution by enabling secure inference directly over encrypted inputs. However, the high computational overhead of HE remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose MOAI, an efficient HE-based, non-interactive framework for secure transformer inference. MOAI gains significant efficiency improvement from: (1) a novel evaluation flow that combines column and diagonal packing with consistent strategies across all layers, eliminating expensive format conversions. (2) rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that significantly reduce the number of costly HE rotations, removing 2,448 HE rotations in BERT-base inference. (3) Column packing removes rotations in plaintext-ciphertext matrix multiplications and interleaved batching further reduces the rotations in ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplications. MOAI uses at least 1.7x fewer HE rotations compared to the state-of-the-art works across all matrix multiplications of BERT-base. As a result, we achieve a $52.8 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to the state-of-the-art HE-based non-interactive secure transformer inference, THOR (Moon et al., CCS 25). We then apply MOAI on the Powerformer's framework and achieve a $55.7 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to Powerformer (Park et al., ACL 25), which approximates Softmax and LayerNorm with simpler functions in transformer and proposes HE-based non-interactive transformer inference. We report an amortized time of 2.36 minutes per input on a single GPU environment. We show the extendibility by applying MOAI in LLaMA-3-8B. Our implementation is publicly available as open source.

BypassGym: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents' Endpoint Defense Evasion Capabilities
BypassGym：一个用于评估AI智能体端点防御规避能力的基准
Weifeng Yuan, Zifan Chen, Yucheng Zhang, Feng Dong, Peng Gao, Haoyu Wang
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Artificial intelligence agents increasingly automate cybersecurity tasks, including offensive operations. Frequent attacks across the web make endpoint detection and response (EDR) a critical defense, but whether AI agents can evade it remains unclear. Benchmarks evaluate the offensive capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents in areas such as penetration testing and vulnerability discovery. One important capability that these benchmarks do not address is defense evasion, specifically whether an agent can develop a program that executes a payload without being blocked or terminated by a deployed EDR. We introduce BypassGym, to our knowledge the first benchmark to systematically evaluate this capability on real endpoints. Given command-and-control (C2) shellcode, an agent must generate and compile a loader that executes the payload without being blocked or terminated. A supplementary evasion knowledge skill provides domain knowledge and supports comparisons with and without this input. BypassGym is built on Proxmox VE(PVE), so the evaluation environment runs real Windows systems and EDR products inside virtual machines and returns structured detection feedback to the agent. We evaluate 5 lightweight model backends against 6 EDR products and 3 payloads, and find that even these simple models generate successful submissions, with DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash reaching 17/18 successful runs and Bitdefender allowing only 5 of 15 runs to pass. These results provide a systematic measurement of current AI agents' endpoint defense evasion capabilities and identify areas for defenders to investigate.

On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
论面向安全多智能体系统的私有知识检索与私有推理
Vicenç Torra, Maria Bras-Amorós
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).
